stories.headline: Kim Zolciak savagely reacts to Kroy Biermann’s makeout with her boyfriend’s ex-wife - Page Six
stories.summary: Biermann and Kyle Mowitz’s ex Jillian Green were photographed packing on the PDA during a hike in Georgia over the weekend.
stories.why: Reality TV drama is collapsing into actual legal/financial chaos—this signals the end of the Housewives era where scandals stayed performative; now they're bankruptcies and restraining orders.

stories.headline: Anatomy of an 11th Edition Codex – What do you get? - Warhammer Community
stories.summary: Look inside Codex: Orks and see what your new book looks like.
stories.why: Warhammer 40K's 11th edition represents the hobby's mainstreaming as a serious competitive/narrative investment, not just basement nerd culture—your buddies are dropping serious money on this.

stories.headline: Taylor Sheridan's Yellowstone Spin-Off 6666 Not Happening At Paramount+ - TVLine
stories.summary: Yellowstone creator Taylor Sheridan will not be wrangling a spin-off for the real-life Four Sixes Ranch.
stories.why: Yellowstone's spin-off collapse shows prestige TV's streaming economics are broken; even creator-driven IP can't justify the budgets anymore, signaling the end of Peak TV abundance.

stories.headline: Amazon seemingly leaked Jason Statham’s entire Mutiny movie - The Verge
stories.summary: The film isn’t supposed to hit theaters for two days, but it was briefly available to stream on Prime Video.
stories.why: Amazon's accidental leak of a major action film days before release exposes how fragile theatrical windows have become—streaming platforms now pose an existential threat to movie theater culture.

stories.headline: Inside Hayden Panettiere’s boyfriend Brian Hickerson’s money troubles after domestic violence arrests - Page Six
stories.summary: The aspiring actor filed for bankruptcy in July 2022, listing assets totaling $25,700 and liabilities totaling around $60,000, according to TMZ.
stories.why: A D-list actor's bankruptcy while dating a famous actress is tabloid standard, but it's trending because it reflects how precarious even marginal entertainment industry income has become.

stories.headline: Christian metal band Demon Hunter sues Netflix over KPop Demon Hunters name - BBC
stories.summary: The band say they face "an existential crisis" after the success of the K-pop-inspired Netflix film.
stories.why: A Christian metal band suing Netflix over a K-pop film name is absurd on surface but signals IP trademark wars are now so expensive that even niche bands must litigate or vanish culturally.

stories.headline: These clever Coyote Vs Acme ads are stopping traffic - Creative Bloq
stories.summary: Acme's catastrophic products have smashed their way into the real world.
stories.why: Ambient advertising breaking into real-world attention (not just social feeds) shows brands are desperate to cut through digital saturation—novelty stunts now compete with actual content.

stories.headline: Rosie O'Donnell thanks Trump in 'Kimmel' monologue - Mashable
stories.summary: "I couldn't have done it without you, sweetie. You brought me back, just like you did with fascism and the measles."
stories.why: A comedian thanking Trump as a career catalyst reveals how polarization has become entertainment's primary fuel; outrage built her comeback, which is the business model now.
